sources.title: Qutb Shahi Heritage Park, Sultan Quli and his garden tomb
sources.note: Direct conservation-project page read. Foundation convention 1518; sixteenth-century stucco and garden enclosure excavations. Do not imply precisely instantaneous sovereignty: the 1518 mosque still acknowledged a Bahmani sovereign.

sources.title: Qutb Shahi Heritage Park, Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah
sources.note: Direct page read: refuge in Vijayanagara, reign1550-1580, Telugu/Persian patronage and original tile remains. Do not imply the Persian Panchatantra adaptation was first composed at this court.

sources.title: Bolakamallaiah, Political Scenario under the Qutub Shahis of Golconda, South Indian History Congress (2015)
sources.note: Direct eight-page PDF read. Only bounded coalition account PDF pages4-5 and late reign dates/conquest pages7-8 used. Internally inconsistent dates, exaggerated harmony/wealth claims, siege length and financial figures omitted.

sources.title: Qutb Shahi Heritage Park, Sultan Muhammad and Hayat Bakshi Begum
sources.note: Direct page read: queen’s family relationships and regency; surviving original glazed tiles and modern restoration. Reconstructed tilework explicitly distinguished from original fragments.

sources.title: Gavin Hambly and Deborah Hutton, Hyderabad, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct full article read. Use early Hyderabad in Monuments and historical conquest1687; internally inconsistent opening dynasty range1490-1686 and early city walls ignored. No modern administrative designation repeated.

sources.title: Qutb Shahi Heritage Park, Hammam conservation
sources.note: Direct project report read. Interconnected cisterns, hot/cold water channels, roof terracotta pipes exposed under modern concrete; interpretation as functional rather than solely funerary bath is a scholarly proposal, explicitly attributed.

sources.title: MIT Libraries, Darushifa, architectural documentation
sources.note: Direct page open failed; full indexed original MIT catalogue text read via query site.dome.mit.edu "Darushifa" "1595". Records1595 patron/date, stone courtyard, patient rooms, bath remains, mosque and former saray. Public paragraph does not claim modern therapeutic efficacy.

sources.title: National Museum New Delhi, Inscribed Hawan-Dasta or Mortar and Pestle, 59.236(a-b)
sources.note: Google Arts and Culture hosts National Museum record. Direct extraction returns interface only; indexed original full catalogue text read with query site.artsandculture.google.com "Inscribed Hawan" "banda". Original Persian inscription in Nastaliq; sample follows museum Roman transcription exactly, not a reconstructed script. Date1600/1700; royal use is curatorial interpretation. Image fetch failed, no claim of independent visual decipherment.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Kalamkari Rumal (Cover), 28.159.1
sources.note: Direct collection record read. Cotton cover attributed to Golconda1640-1650; courtly scenes; inventory notationNovember-December1673 at Amber. Date of inventory is not manufacture date.

sources.title: IGNOU, Theme III, Case Study: Masulipatnam
sources.note: Same official PDF downloaded/read in Bijapur packet. Printed p240/PDF86 supports weaving villages and chaya-root dye. Budget explicitly combined with 153 words in Bijapur; new paragraph is short.

sources.title: British Museum, Court scene with Sultan Abdullah Qutub Shah, 1974,0617,0.6.1
sources.note: Full indexed institutional record read; direct canonical open failed. Date about1630; attendants, dancers, musicians and vizier; later bound in1643 Diwan of Hafiz, which does not date painting. No inscription on painting.

proposedOverrides.summary: Golconda’s Qutb Shahi rulers built an influential Deccan kingdom and the city of Hyderabad.

batchIdentityNotes.historicalIdentity: Qutb Shahi Sultanate of Golconda/Hyderabad, conventionally1518-1687
batchIdentityNotes.interpretation: Earlier snapshots are virtually fixed regional approximations and start before conventional dynastic independence; final1650-1700 polygon expands south and east. Public overview warns coverage is not dynasty lifetime. Later golconda1783-1800 deliberately excluded as a different historical phase.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceDisagreement: Founder transition is conventionally1518; a1518 mosque still names the Bahmani sovereign. Avoid an instantaneous independence ceremony or invented exact founding day. Iranica opening dynasty range is inconsistent; use heritage-project chronology and its independently explicit1687 conquest.
